## [Awarding XP:]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:16pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.on19n0wlx73n style="padding-top:18pt;margin:0;color:#000000;padding-left:0;font-size:16pt;padding-bottom:6pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [XP will not just be awarded for defeating enemies combat, but also
    for the
    following]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Completing Quests (main or side
    quests)]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Engaging with the story
    events]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Social
    Encounters]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Puzzles]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   Avoiding combat or causing the enemies to flee
-   [Saving Shared Destiny points (see
    inspiration)]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```

    unless you write a story about what your character was doing and how
    they also gained XP while away from the group. This story must be
    read aloud at the start of the next
    session.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

## [Inspiration:]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:16pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.iw7o72g2tdck style="padding-top:18pt;margin:0;color:#000000;padding-left:0;font-size:16pt;padding-bottom:6pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [Shared
    Destiny]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   At the start of each session, the whole party starts with 4 Shared
    Destiny points. Each Shared Destiny Point can be used according to
    the following table: similarly to Heroic Inspiration, allowing a
    reroll of any D20 test. Additionally, if a character instantly dies
    to an attack or if they fail their 3rd death saving throw, 4 Shared
    Destiny points can be used to instantly stabilize that character and
    prevent their death. Other alternate uses listed below
-   [At the end of each session, any left over SD points are converted
    to XP, as per the table
    below.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

    for more experienced players. These are merely suggestions, feel
    free to ask to use a different class's trade off or create an
    entirely new one. Make sure to talk to me before applying or picking
    any of

    mastery properties for multiple weapons, you instead use the mastery
    of just one type of weapon. When you do so, you gain a +1 bonus to
    attack and damage rolls with that weapon. Additionally you can add
    either the Push or Vex properties to the chosen weapon. You may only
    activate one mastery property at a time with this feature. You may
    not use mastery properties of any other weapon and you have a -1 to
    attack and damage rolls with other weapons.
    ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}


    at all costs. Whenever you drop a creature to 0 hit points with your
    attacks, it falls unconscious rather than dying outright. You cannot
    initiate a fight, and you cannot call others to strike in your
    stead. Due to this oath, you are well respected and have advantage
    on checks to negotiate peace and


    social checks while out in the wilderness. This includes checks to
    interact with animals, woodland creatures, or other forest dwellers.
    Alternatively, you are uncomfortable in large cities, gaining
    Disadvantage on all social checks when in large


-   [You can sense when someone is watching you, with the feeling
    growing more intense based on how closely you are being tracked.
    This has the downside of making you paranoid. If you are ever on
    guard or on watch alone, you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw
    with a DC equal to 10 + your Proficiency Bonus, or freak out and
    become incapable of doing meaningful work until you finish a Short
    or Long Rest. While freaking out, you have Disadvantage on all
    ability checks and attack
    rolls.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

    component costs. After doing so, your hit point maximum is reduced
    by that amount until you finish a long rest. This rule applies to
    any material components with a listed gold piece cost, whether or

## [Resting:]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:16pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.5kpg75wcy8dm style="padding-top:18pt;margin:0;color:#000000;padding-left:0;font-size:16pt;padding-bottom:6pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

[Short rests take 8 hours, 6 of which must be dedicated to sleep. The
other 2 hours can be dedicated to light activity such as reading, taking
watch, crafting,
etc.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[Long rests may only happen in designated areas such as towns,
settlements, or fortified structures and take 24 hours of sleep and
light activity. Light activity consists of any activity that is not too
demanding on the adventurer. Socializing, shopping, studying, and
crafting are some examples of light activity. A Long Rest is broken if
you cast a level 1+ spell, engage in combat, or leave the settlement you
are resting in. If a Long Rest is broken, the character gains the
benefits of a Short Rest if at least 8 hours have already passed during
the rest.
]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[Based on the location, there is a certain GP cost per person to rest.
This is a combination of food, lodging, and any other expenses, such as
stables for horses. This cost is location specific, and usually depends
on the wealth of the location and the amenities
provided.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[Due to the lengthier rest time, any ability or spell which lasts for 8
hours will instead last until the next long rest. One prominent example
of this is the Mage Armor
spell.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Falling:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.iprje118qwpg style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

Whenever a creature would fall 10 ft or more, the creature could choose
to delay its fall until the end of its next turn, or the end of its
current turn, whichever comes first (a.k.a Coyote Time). When a creature
hits the ground it takes 1d6 damage for every 10ft that it falls up to a
maximum of 150d6. A creature falls 500 ft per round unless slowed by
magic or some special ability.

### [Flanking:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.78rzrl8pcs8u style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   Flanking an enemy grants a +2 to attack rolls.[ To count as flanking
    a creature, at least one of its allies must be adjacent to an enemy
    and on opposite sides or corners of the enemy's
    space.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   When in doubt about whether two creatures flank an enemy on a grid,
    trace an imaginary line between the centers of the creatures'
    spaces. If the line passes through opposite sides or corners of the
    enemy's space, the enemy is
    flanked.[![](data:image/png;base64,){style="width: 624.00px; height: 201.00px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);"}]{style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 218.00px; height: 201.00px;"}

### [Pushing Creatures Into Walls and Other Solid Objects]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.6ujlh67zzcom style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [If a creature is moved by a spell or ability into a wall or another
    creature, it takes damage proportional to the remaining amount they
    would have been pushed. For each 5 extra feet the creature would
    have been pushed, it takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage. If the creature
    is pushed into another creature, both creatures take the full
    damage.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Example 1: A battlemaster fighter uses pushing attack to push an
    enemy goblin backwards. The goblin flies 5 feet backwards and then
    hits a solid wall. Since the goblin would have moved 10 more feet if
    the wall wasn't there, he instead takes 2d4 bludgeoning
    damage.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Example 2: A Warlock uses a repelling blast to push a zombie into
    the necromancer standing 5 feet behind it. The zombie flies back 5
    feet and then hits the necromancer. Since the zombie would have
    traveled 5 more feet both the necromancer and the zombie each take
    1d4 bludgeoning damage.
    ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Sweep/Cleave attacks:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.1smgckybv83v style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [When you reduce a creature to zero hit points with a weapon attack,
    you can divert any remaining damage to an additional creature of
    your choice, provided you are proficient with the weapon and your
    initial attack roll also hits the chosen creature. For melee weapon
    attacks, the target must be in reach. For ranged weapon attacks:
    Target must be in range and in a straight
    line]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Push Beyond Your Limits:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.jaqruuc0pxxw style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [If you are out of spell slots but still want to cast a spell, then
    you can push beyond your limits, casting a spell without a spell
    slot, but taking one level of exhaustion per spell slot level. If
    you cast a spell of 6th level or higher in this was, consult the
    following
    table]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   []{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [Spell Level]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}   [Effect]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [6]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}             [Immediately fall to 0 hit points and take one death saving throw failure.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [7]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}             [Immediately Die.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [8]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}             [Immediately Die, only a spell of level 7 or above can bring you back to life]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [9]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}             [Immediately Die. Nothing short of True Resurrection or a Wish spell can bring you back to life]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### [Spell Rulings:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.82b8p4p83pwu style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [Counterspell and Dispel Magic will be run using the following
    method]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [If the spell being countered is equal to or less than the level of
    the spell slot used for counterspell, the original spell has no
    effect and the action used to cast it is wasted, along with any
    resource or spell slot used is
    wasted.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [If the spell being countered is greater than the level of the spell
    slot used for counterspell, then the counterspell caster must make a
    check using their spell casting ability (no proficiency) against a
    DC = 10 + the spells level. The counterspeller can gain a bonus to
    this check equal to the level of spell slot above 3 that they use to
    cast
    counterspell.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [For example, if a wizard is trying to counter a level 5 Cone of
    Cold spell with a level 4 Counterspell, the wizard has to roll a
    d20 + their Intelligence modifier + 1 (for using a 4th level spell
    slot, which is one above 3). The wizard would need to beat a DC of
    15, which is 10 + 5 (the level of the
    spell)]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Inflict
    wounds]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [We will use the 2014 version of this
    spell]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Spell Durations:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.5v1rknw2rvcs style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [Any spell lasting 8 hours will now instead last until the next long
    rest]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Spell Scrolls:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.h5rurbc9t4w0 style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

[Anyone can use spell scrolls regardless of class, but doing so might
have unintended side effects. If the spell scroll being used is not on
your class list, then make an Arcana check. The DC for this check is
10 + the spell's level. If you roll 10 less than the DC, a wild magic
surge is triggered. If your roll is 10 higher than the spell's DC, the
spell is cast and the spell scroll can be used
again.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

## [Stealth: ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:16pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.q05j22muyeei style="padding-top:18pt;margin:0;color:#000000;padding-left:0;font-size:16pt;padding-bottom:6pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [A stealth operation happens in multiple phases. Most operations
    start in the hidden phase. Some may start in the searching phase, if
    the enemy is expecting the party:
    ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Hidden]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [The group makes a group stealth check as they are moving around, if
    the group check beats the passive perception of the enemy, they
    continue unnoticed. Otherwise, the enemy begins to
    search.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [If the party is infiltrating, or is unexpected, they start
    here]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Searching]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [The enemy is not fully aware of your presence, but they begin to
    make perception checks to try and figure out what the disturbance
    is. The group rerolls a group stealth check contested with the
    enemy's group perception check. Failing causes the enemy to see
    you.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [If the party is escaping a group of enemies, they start in this
    phase]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Seen]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [The enemy notices the group and acts
    accordingly]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Surprise]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [If the group attacks before the seen phase, they get surprise
    against the enemy (see surprise in the combat
    section)]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

[]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[Archive
Rules:]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:26pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

[Rules that I have written but am not currently using or may only use on
occasion.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Morale Checks:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.xl4x77g2cfse style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [The DM may choose to do a morale check when the enemies are
    outnumbered, surprised, or losing numbers quickly. Have the leader
    of the enemies (or the most powerful if they are unorganized) make a
    Wisdom check. If the check equals or exceeds the DC, the enemies
    pass the morale check and continue to fight. The DC is calculated
    using the following formula, but may have additional modifiers based
    on the
    situation.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [DC = 10 - \# of enemies alive + \# of players that are not
    unconscious.
    ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Any additional situation modifiers should be applied using the
    following rule: Any positive modifiers make it more difficult for
    the enemies to stick around, while negative modifiers make it easier
    for the enemies to stick around. Examples are listed
    below]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   []{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [Situation]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                                                      [Modifier]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The enemies were surprised]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                                     [+1]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The enemies have lost a key combatant]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                          [+2]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The players passed an intimidation check against the enemies]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}   [+1]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The players landed a critical hit]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                              [+1]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The players were surprised]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                                     [-1]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The enemies landed a critical hit]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}                              [-1]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The enemies are significantly stronger than the players]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}        [-3]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  [The enemies are significantly weaker than the players]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}          [+3]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### [Weapon sizes:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.ul6tt19fpn28 style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [Damage dice progression when increasing
    size]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [1 \> 1d4 \> 1d6 \> 1d8/2d4 \> 1d10 \> 1d12/2d6 \> 2d8 \> 2d10 \>
    2d12 \>
    3d8]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [When using an oversized weapon you have disadvantage on attacks
    with that weapon if you are one size smaller than the creature it
    was designed for. If you are two sizes smaller, then you are not
    able to wield such a large weapon. Additionally if you grow or
    shrink in size possibly due to an enlarge/reduce spell, your weapon
    damage increases by one size for every size category you go up. When
    you shrink your weapon damage also goes down by one size for every
    size category you
    shrink.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [Your reach increases by 5ft for every size category you go up and
    decreases to a minimum of 5ft for every size category you
    shrink.]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

### [Casting Multiple Spells on a Turn:]{style="color:#434343;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:14pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"} {#h.wwbhrndxw6pz style="padding-top:16pt;margin:0;color:#434343;padding-left:0;font-size:14pt;padding-bottom:4pt;line-height:1.15;page-break-after:avoid;font-family:\"Arial\";orphans:2;widows:2;text-align:left;padding-right:0"}

-   [Note: This is actually identical to the default rules in 2024, thus
    moved to
    archive]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [A caster can cast multiple spells on a turn if they meet any of the
    following
    requirements]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [Players: Only one spell uses a spell
    slot]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   [EX: A druid casting Spike growth (action) and a shillelagh (bonus
    action)]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
-   [EX: A drow cleric casting healing word (bonus action) and using the
    darkness spell (action) from their species features.
    ]{style="color:#000000;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;font-size:11pt;font-family:\"Arial\";font-style:normal"}
